description: T1.1 — High-precision test of cyFlQ-agent hypothesis: Δm_{n-p} ?= m_e · Σ_3 where Σ_3 = Σ_{λ⊢3} 1/dim_q V_λ = 2 + 1/[2]_q (Frobenius co-Casimir at n=3). Verified at 50 dps using repo-canonical q_0 from q_parameter.Q and CODATA 2022 m_e, m_p, m_n. Result: predicted Δm = 1.27611 MeV vs CODATA 1.29333 MeV; rel. err = -1.331 %, residual = -26 555 σ on CODATA Δm uncertainty. Hypothesis FALSIFIED in its simplest form — match is structural/leading-order only, not exact. Higher-tower correction of order 1.3 % is required to close the gap.
interpretation: m_e · Σ_3 captures the leading order of Δm_{n-p} (gets 98.67%) but is 1.33% short. The 26 554 σ residual rules out any reading where this is an exact identity. The same magnitude (~1.27 MeV) coincidentally appears in three places: (i) Δm_{n-p}, (ii) the proton tower residual prop:partition-sum-proton-residual, (iii) m_e · Σ_3. All three agree to ~1 % but not better. Closing the 1.33 % gap requires higher-tower or pair-generator corrections, not just the Σ_3 sum. The 'one extra Frobenius co-Casimir' picture is approximately right but quantitatively incomplete.
next_steps: Compute Δm via Markov-invariant pair-generator tower (canonical_isospin_pyhecke + antipode-symmetrised V̂); see if pair correction closes the 1.33% gap.
Check whether prop:partition-sum-proton-residual gives 1.27611 MeV at 50 dps independent of m_e·Σ_3; if so the two are the same algebraic object and the gap is real.
Test alt hypothesis: Δm_{n-p} = m_e · Σ_3 · (1 + h^2/[2]_q^2) where h = q - q^{-1} — check whether O(h^2) tower correction matches the missing 1.33%.
